Article Title: Akal Takht panel asks Punjab govt to address objections before anti-sacrilege talks
Article Text:
Akal Takht panel flags Punjab govt response, seeks compliance report on anti-sacrilege law

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The expert panel appointed by the Akal Takht on Friday asked the Punjab government to first submit a compliance report on the objections raised by the Sikh temporal seat before any further talks on the proposed anti-sacrilege law.The panel, formed to discuss the Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026 with the state government, held its first meeting on Thursday.The panel said the Punjab government's July 29 response did not address the main concerns raised by the Akal Takht, especially those related to possible interference in Sikh religious matters.On June 29, Akal Takht Jathedar Giani Kuldip Singh Gargajj had given the state government one month to respond to his objections to the anti-sacrilege law.In a statement on Friday, the Akal Takht secretariat said the government's response, submitted just before the deadline, was an attempt to avoid the main issues. It said the concerns of the Sikh community had already been conveyed to the Punjab assembly Speaker and members of the state Cabinet on July 31.The secretariat also accused the Bhagwant Mann-led government of not taking a constructive approach towards resolving the sensitive issue.It said that despite being given enough time, the Punjab government had not formed its own panel to discuss the matter.Earlier, Jathedar Gargajj had rejected the government's response as "unsatisfactory" and announced a five-member expert panel to hold discussions with the Aam Aadmi Party government.The panel includes retired judges Rupinder Singh Sodhi and Mohinder Mohan Singh Bedi, senior advocate Puran Singh Hundal, and Sikh scholars Dr Kehar Singh and Prof Jagmohan Singh.The Jathedar had also written to Punjab assembly Speaker Kultar Singh, Sikh MLAs and state ministers, asking them not to discuss or amend the anti-sacrilege law without a wider "Panthic" consensus.He had directed Sikh MLAs and Cabinet ministers to ensure that no discussion on the law takes place during the assembly session that began on August 3 until an agreement is reached with the Akal Takht and the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC).The issue came up after AAP MLA Inderbir Singh Nijjar submitted the Punjab government's response to the objections raised by the Akal Takht over the proposed anti-sacrilege legislation.
Article Summary: The panel said the Punjab government's July 29 response did not address the main concerns raised by the Akal Takht. The panel, formed to discuss the Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026 with the state government, held its first meeting on Thursday.

Article Title: 17.4 lakh blood components discarded in 2025 despite record collection
Article Text:
India discarded over 17.4 lakh blood components in 2025

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India discarded over 17.4 lakh blood components in 2025, even as blood collection reached a record 1.58 crore units, according to state-wise data tabled in the Rajya Sabha, highlighting continued challenges in blood inventory management despite a steady rise in donations.Available official data indicate that China and India are among the world's largest blood collection programmes. In 2025, India collected 15.71 million units of blood, while China collected 25.5 million units, according to China's National Health Commission.The data, reported by blood centres through the government's e-Raktakosh portal, show that expiry was the leading reason for discarding blood components, followed by reactive units and other operational reasons. Reason-wise discard data has been captured on the portal since 2024, while such details were not available for 2023.Replying to a question in Parliament, the Union health ministry, however, said it had not received any report of regional blood shortages. It added that ensuring an adequate supply of safe blood and minimising wastage is primarily the responsibility of state governments and Union Territories, while the Centre advocates a hub-and-spoke model under which blood is collected and processed at high-volume centres before being distributed to smaller blood banks and storage centres.According to the data, Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest blood collection in 2025 with 21.6 lakh units, followed by Maharashtra (18.73 lakh), Gujarat (11.82 lakh), Rajasthan (10.79 lakh) and Tamil Nadu (9.74 lakh). Overall blood collection increased from 1.42 crore units in 2023 to 1.58 crore units in 2025.The annexure also showed a corresponding increase in blood component utilisation, with Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan reporting the highest utilisation during 2025.At the same time, Uttar Pradesh reported the highest discard of blood components at 2.40 lakh, followed by Maharashtra (1.87 lakh), Kerala (1.44 lakh), Rajasthan (1.21 lakh) and Tamil Nadu (1.09 lakh). The ministry did not provide an analysis of the wide variation in discard across states.Dr Hema Goyal, Consultant (Blood centre & Lab services), Aakash healthcare said blood wastage is inevitable to some extent, particularly because platelets have a shelf life of only five days. But discarding 17.4 lakh blood components in a year points to a mismatch between collection and actual demand. The solution is not fewer donations but smarter inventory management through real-time stock sharing and better coordination between blood banks.
Article Summary: India discarded over 17.4 lakh blood components in 2025. Blood collection reached a record 1.58 crore units, according to state-wise data tabled in the Rajya Sabha. Expiry was the leading reason for discarding blood, followed by reactive units.

Article Title: FSSAI pulls up two popular food products over safety, compliance lapses
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: In a fresh crackdown on food safety violations, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has acted against two food products, penalising the manufacturer of a fortified sunflower oil after it was found to be substandard and stopping the sale of a Monk Fruit Sweetener over alleged licensing and labelling violations.The regulator imposed a penalty on AWL Agri Business Ltd, Mangaluru, after a laboratory analysis of a retail sample of Fortune "Fryola" Refined Sunflower Seed Oil found that its vitamin D content was below the prescribed standard, making the fortified edible oil substandard under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.FSSAI said the company was given an opportunity to present its case, but the adjudicating authority concluded that it had manufactured and marketed a substandard fortified edible oil before imposing a monetary penalty.In a separate action, the regulator prohibited the sale of PIE Foods' Monk Fruit Sweetener, a natural zero-calorie sugar substitute, after inspections found cartons of the product stored at the company's premises without the required manufacturing licence.FSSAI also alleged that the product carried claims such as "100% Monk Fruit Extract" and "Natural Ingredients", while its online listing did not carry the mandatory endorsement required under food safety regulations.It further said the company failed to produce records showing that the monk fruit extract used in the product had been procured in accordance with the Food Safety and Standards Act.The prohibition order will remain in force until the product complies with the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act and related regulations.The regulator said the actions are part of its ongoing drive to tighten enforcement against food business operators and ensure that products sold to consumers meet prescribed safety and quality standards.
Article Summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has acted against two food products. The regulator penalised the manufacturer of a fortified sunflower oil after it was found to be substandard. It also stopped the sale of a Monk Fruit Sweetener over alleged licensing and labelling violations.

Article Title: Om Birla seeks proposal for Makar Dwar porch
Article Text:
Officials said this is necessary considering that MPs arriving and leaving the new Parliament House wait for their vehicles out in the open

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has asked CPWD officials and its architects to consider the feasibility and submit a proposal for the construction of a porch at Makar Dwar, which is mostly used by members of Parliament to enter and exit the complex.The plan of the porch would address the inconvenience caused to MPs and other staff, particularly when it rains.At present, the entrance is uncovered, unlike other “dwars” that the Speaker, Rajya Sabha chairman and PM use. Central Public Works Department (CPWD) will carry out a feasibility exercise to add a porch over this entrance. Officials said this is necessary considering that MPs arriving and leaving the new Parliament House wait for their vehicles out in the open. The government has not yet disclosed the exact cost of the project, which has reportedly escalated to around Rs 1,300 crore.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has asked CPWD officials and its architects to consider the feasibility and submit a proposal. The plan of the porch would address the inconvenience caused to MPs and other staff, particularly when it rains. The government has not yet disclosed the exact cost of the project, which has reportedly escalated to around Rs 1,300 crore.

Article Title: UPI charges: Lok Sabha passes bill for government to make changes
Article Text:
The FM said the charge will apply to merchants and not to users and will help banks and fintech invest in infrastructure and innovation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha on Thursday passed a Bill that seeks to ease tax rules to attract investments and remove the existing legal provision that prevents banks and payment service providers from charging Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on notified electronic payment modes.The Bill — passed without discussion amid din — also proposes to remove the linkage between the Payment and Settlement Systems Act and the I-Tax Act and give legal backing to the government to modify the zero-MDR framework on UPI and RuPay card transactions. Outside the House, however, there was an exchange between FM Nirmala Sitharaman and Congress MP Jairam Ramesh. Ramesh said the Bill opens the doors for MDR. The FM responded, saying the charge will apply to merchants and not to users and will help banks and fintech invest in infrastructure and innovation.“More importantly, the UPI and services steering committee headed by NPCI is yet to decide on the MDR. This will happen after Parliament passes the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026... All this could have been discussed on the floor of the House if your party @INCIndia (Congress) engages constructively in Parliament when the Bill was/is tabled,” she said.While leaving person-to-payments outside MDR’s ambit, banks and fintechs may be permitted to charge 0.25% to 0.4% on payments to businesses in excess of Rs 2,000 with an overall ceiling on how much can be charged.Officials have argued that the levy will be lower than what is charged on credit and debit cards, and most merchants will not pass it on to consumers.
Article Summary: The Bill also proposes to remove the linkage between the Payment and Settlement Systems Act and the I-Tax Act. Outside the House, there was an exchange between FM Nirmala Sitharaman and Congress MP Jairam Ramesh. The FM said the charge will apply to merchants and not to users.

Article Title: Rahul ignored plan to end my fast, says Sonam Wangchuk
Article Text:
Wangchuk also accused JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh of breaking a promise not to release photos of them offering him soup until he could announce the end of his fast

NEW DELHI: Sonam Wangchuk said his wife Gitanjali had tried to get Rahul Gandhi to offer him juice to end his 26-day hunger strike at Jantar Mantar but received no positive response, leaving him disappointed with the Congress leader and other political parties."We were pondering on breaking my fast through Rahul Gandhi ji and Gitanjali was working on that," Wangchuk told India Today. "She was working hard to see if Rahul ji could break my fast. She didn't get a positive response".Wangchuk also accused Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh of breaking a promise not to release photos of them offering him soup until he could announce the end of his fast with opposition and student leaders represented. "They pledged they won't release it and they broke the promise. So I have lost trust in all these leaders," he said.Wangchuk said his wife's subsequent criticism of Rahul had stemmed partly from his own disappointment. He also said netas had come to the Jantar Mantar agitation in small numbers and late. "Similarly, as I said, at Jantar Mantar very few and very late came, so this disappointment caught on her when she made a single comment about them," he added.Gitanjali was targeted online after questioning Rahul's decision to stage a protest outside the PM's residence. Wangchuk said she had made several strong comments against BJP and Hindutva forces as well, but while they kept quiet, the Congress "ecosystem" turned on her for criticising Gandhi."There were four or five very harsh comments about BJP. They didn't react, but the (Congress) ecosystem started trolling her, trolling me," he said. "I am disappointed with the leadership. They shouldn't be so narrow in their approach."Wangchuk, however, was supportive of CJP, whose agitation against examination irregularities he joined at Jantar Mantar. He said he had studied the organisation and found its members "very well-meaning, fair and just and for the right cause, not aligned to any party as such".He welcomed CJP's decision to remain an apolitical pressure group instead of contesting polls. "Being apolitical, it gives voice to the voiceless," he said, adding that this had been his advice to its leadership.
Article Summary: Sonam Wangchuk said his wife Gitanjali had tried to get Rahul Gandhi to offer him juice to end his 26-day hunger strike at Jantar Mantar. Wangchuk also accused Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh of breaking a promise not to release photos of them offering him soup.

Article Title: Tarun Tejpal sentenced to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment in 2013 rape case; gets two weeks to surrender
Article Text:
Bombay HC convicts Tarun Tejpal in 2013 rape case, sentences him to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment

PANAJI: Thirteen years after the arrest of a high profile editor-in-chief of Tehelka magazine, Tarun Tejpal , for rape in an elevator of a starred hotel, the Bombay high court on Thursday found him guilty of rape and sentenced him to ten years Rigorous imprisonment.The HC has granted him two weeks time to surrender.The sentence was pronounced in the State's challenge to Tejpal's acquittal by the trial court in 2021.After the court found him guilty, senior advocate Aabad Ponda representing Tejpal sought lenient sentence for him on the grounds that he is a senior citizen today, aged 62 and that the case is a 13 year old one.Tejpal addressing the division bench of Justices Dr Neela Gokhale and Amit Jamsandekar said he is a "political victim" and is 62 years old and a father of two with a wife and sought a lenient sentence.He said that there is so much evidence in favour of him that he can be acquitted ten times.Solicitor general of India representing Goa Government Tushar Mehta however argued for maximum sentence for Tejpal. He urged the court to consider that Tejpal was old enough to be in a parental position vis-a vis the survivor and argued that the sentence should set a precedent and have a strong deterrent effect.Mehta said that this was not some "misunderstanding or some banter" and pointed out that Tejpal had no remorse after the incident and alleged that he repeated the same thing on the next day.He said Tejpal was brazen despite resistance and despite the survivor saying no.He further argued that the survivor's mature conduct after the incident had been wrongly portrayed as that of someone who had enjoyed the molestation."It is high time the highest constitutional court of the state gives him the maximum sentence. No means No. You may be whosoever you are but when a girl says no it means no. That deterrent message may be considered," Mehta told the court while arguing on maximum sentence for him.Mehta during the hearings seeking Tejpal's conviction argued that the survivor was a stellar witness and stood by her case and that Tejpal's apology to her was proof of what he had done. He also argued that there was no reason for a man of her father's age to send her such her the 'the fingertips' text message after midnight and that it could not reasonably have an innocent meaning. Ponda had countered that saying the 'fingertips' text message had a different context and did not prove charge of rape.He had argued that the survivor had a "propensity to lie" and that her behaviour after the alleged incident was not commensurate with someone who had been raped and traumatised.
Article Summary: Bombay HC convicts Tarun Tejpal in 2013 rape case, sentences him to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment. The HC has granted him two weeks time to surrender. After the court found him guilty, senior advocate Aabad Ponda sought lenient sentence for him.

Article Title: Government maps 27 Arunachal border locations with standard names
Article Text:
Several of the named sites on the map carry the weight of India-China conflict.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

GUWAHATI/NEW DELHI: The updated Survey of India map has assigned standard place and feature names to 27 Arunachal Pradesh sites, including four mountain passes and a high-altitude lake, as part of the Union government’s strategy to remove any ambiguity on demarcation of territory and counter China’s repeated attempts to rename places on this side of the McMahon Line.The MHA said on Friday that the names were finalised in consultation with the Arunachal Pradesh government. “Identifying them formally on the Survey of India map is aimed at facilitating their accurate recognition and better awareness among the public.”Of the 27 sites identified on the map, one is a monument. Three of the rest — Longju, Maja & Bisa — are strategically important border villages in Upper Subansiri district. There are also three passes along the McMahon Line, Dzo La, Riza La and Pukur La, in the same district. Thag La pass, a 1962 battleground, lies on the border in Tawang district.“These places are already marked on Indian military maps, even those of 1962 vintage. Identifying them on Survey of India maps is a bold counter to China,” a source said.Several of the named sites carry the weight of India-China conflict. Longju was one of the earliest flashpoints in the boundary dispute and was occupied by Chinese troops in 1959.Thag La overlooks Namka Chu valley, where the 1962 conflict began after Chinese forces crossed the McMahon Line.Jaswant Garh, in Tawang, commemorates Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat, one of the most celebrated heroes of 1962 war. The Sher-e-Thapa Memorial in Upper Subansiri honours Hav Shere Thapa, whose resistance at Rio Bridge significantly delayed the Chinese advance in 1962. The lone lake named is Sambho Sarovar, a high-altitude glacial lake.The remaining land areas include Bara Kundun, Chhota Kundun and Dhan Bari in Anjaw district; Pritnagar, Buddhamandir, Jairampur, Teritnagar and Ramnagar in Changlang; Sagar, Padma, Jyotinagar and Baisakhi in West Kameng; Chhota Ropuk and Bara Ropuk in Upper Subansiri; and Shivaji Nagar, Sunpura and Kamlang Nagar in Lohit.In April, China announced Chinese names for 23 locations in Arunachal Pradesh, which Beijing refers to as “South Tibet”. The external affairs ministry then said assigning “fictitious names” wouldn’t alter the reality that Arunachal Pradesh “was, is, and will always remain an integral and inalienable part of India”. China has carried out similar renaming exercises periodically.McMahon Line demarcates the boundary between India and China in the eastern sector, separating Arunachal from Tibet.
Article Summary: The updated Survey of India map has assigned standard place and feature names to 27 Arunachal Pradesh sites. The names are part of the Union government’s strategy to remove any ambiguity on demarcation of territory. China has repeated attempts to rename places on this side of the McMahon Line.

Article Title: Delhi high court stays food regulator's ban on certain Dabur products
Article Text:
The HC issued a notice to FSSAI on the company's petition challenging the prohibition

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court on Friday stayed an FSSAI directive prohibiting Dabur India from selling food products such as honey, cow ghee and edible oils with "100%" claims.Justice Amit Mahajan noted that Dabur was selling the products for decades and had shown a prima facie case for relief at this stage, as the FSSAI issued the order without granting a hearing to the company.The HC issued notice to FSSAI on Dabur's petition challenging the prohibition and asked it to file its reply before the next date, while listing the matter for hearing on Aug 24.Dabur argued that the FSSAI order was in violation of principles of natural justice. It also submitted that the expression "100%" is used by many players.
Article Summary: Delhi high court stays an FSSAI directive prohibiting Dabur India from selling food products with "100%" claims. Justice Amit Mahajan noted that Dabar was selling the products for decades and had shown a prima facie case for relief at this stage. The HC issued a notice to FSSAi on the company's petition challenging the prohibition.

Article Title: Air India salary hikes salaries of pilots by up to 15%
Article Text:
Air India is restoring international flights that were slashed post the West Asia crisis and will return to Jan-Feb levels next month

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Air India on Friday hiked pilot salaries by 8% to 15%, with commanders getting the biggest hikes and increases tapering by rank. Going ahead, first officers or co-pilots will get command upgrades in AI Express, which has single-aisle aircraft, then move to AI, which has wide-body aircraft with higher pay, to build progression within the group. Air India has tried to make Air India Express more attractive through better pay and to address shortages on the B737 fleet.Air India pilots have for years been facing a 40-hour guaranteed pay — meaning they get minimum pay for these hours irrespective of actual flying, while flying more means more pay — while IndiGo has fixed pay for 70 hours. Under the revised framework, Air India will continue to provide guaranteed pay for 40 flying hours but has enhanced flying allowance rates. Rates beyond 40 hours have been increased, aligning compensation with industry benchmarks while rewarding productivity.Air India is restoring international flights that were slashed post the West Asia crisis and will return to Jan-Feb levels next month. Pakistan airspace closure means longer routes, higher flying time and greater pilot requirements.A senior commander flying 55 hours a month will get Rs 8.3 lakh, up from Rs 7.5 lakh, while a first officer will get Rs 3.3 lakh, up from just over Rs 3 lakh.Privilege leave has been reduced from 30 to 24 days, though weekly offs will not be counted as leave.Since Tata Group took over Air India and Air India Express in Jan 2022, it has grown from around 100 to 300 aircraft. Under the new framework, Air India Express will serve as the “primary pathway” for command upgrades. They can then progress to Air India for wide-body flying. A fleet allowance is being offered to pilots supporting the B737 fleet in Air India Express.
Article Summary: Air India on Friday hiked pilot salaries by 8% to 15%, with commanders getting the biggest hikes and increases tapering by rank. First officers or co-pilots will get command upgrades in AI Express, then move to AI, which has wide-body aircraft with higher pay. Air India has tried to make Air India Express more attractive through better pay and to address shortages on the B737 fleet.

Article Title: Supreme Court shunts out two coal scam judges on unusual Delhi high court request
Article Text:
On Friday, Delhi HC issued the consequential transfer and posting orders for judges Sunena Sharma and Dheeraj Mor

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Barely six months after appointing a sessions judge to exclusively hear coal scam cases in Delhi, Supreme Court has replaced her, acting on an unusual request from the Delhi high court, which said she and another special CBI judge were “better suited for certain other responsibilities”.A bench of Chief Justice Suryakant and Justices Joymala Bagchi and V Mohana, in an order, recorded that Delhi high court had sought the transfer of special judges Sunena Sharma and Dheeraj Mor so they could be assigned other responsibilities.Sharma had assumed charge in January after SC approved Delhi HC’s request to relieve then incumbent Sanjay Bansal, who had presided over the special coal scam court for nearly four-and-a-half years. Mor was appointed special judge in April 2025. The latest request came with Sharma barely six months into her tenure and Mor having completed just over a year in the post.SC noted that it had received a letter from the registrar general of Delhi HC stating that Sharma and Mor were “better suited for certain other responsibilities”. The HC also described both judicial officers as “of outstanding merit” and said it wished to utilise their services elsewhere.Accepting the request, the top court permitted Delhi high court to transfer Sharma and Mor from the posts of special judges hearing CBI coal scam cases. It also approved the appointment of Virender Kumar Kharta, earlier special judge of the NDPS court at Saket, and Ajay Garg, previously an additional sessions judge at a fast-track court in Tis Hazari, as their replacements. Kharta will succeed Sharma, while Garg will take over from Mor.On Friday, Delhi HC issued the consequential transfer and posting orders. Interestingly, neither Sharma nor Mor has been assigned a fresh judicial posting. According to the notification, both have been attached to the office of the principal district and sessions judge (CBI).The high court directed both officers to notify all matters in which judgments or orders had been reserved before relinquishing charge and pronounce them on the scheduled date or, at the latest, within two to three weeks despite the transfer. The dates fixed for pronouncement must also be reflected in the cause lists of both the previous and new courts, as well as on the court’s website.Last year, 29 CBI corruption cases were pending before two special coal scam courts, while more than 27 had already been disposed of.
Article Summary: Delhi high court had sought the transfer of special judges Sunena Sharma and Dheeraj Mor so they could be assigned other responsibilities. Sharma assumed charge in January after SC approved Delhi HC’s request to relieve then incumbent Sanjay Bansal, who had presided over the special coal scam court for nearly four-and-a-half years.

Article Title: Share data on river waters, India tells China
Article Text:
The 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation & Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC) on Thursday saw both sides agreeing to continue using existing diplomatic and military channels

NEW DELHI: In another round of diplomatic engagement on the border issue, India and China had “frank discussions” and reviewed the situation along the line of actual control (LAC), with the former underlining that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the development of bilateral relations.The Indian side also reiterated the need for early convening of the next meeting of the Expert Level Mechanism on trans-border rivers, which was established in 2006, and emphasised the importance of sharing technical details on upstream projects.Following the recent announcement of a mega dam project by China, India has been raising the need for transparency and consultation with downstream countries on such upstream activities.According to the Indian govt, as a lower riparian state with established user rights to the waters of trans-border rivers, India routinely conveys its views and concerns to the Chinese authorities, and has urged them to ensure that the interests of downstream states are not harmed by activities in upstream areas. India has repeatedly stressed resumption of the provision of hydrological data and other cooperation pertaining to trans-border rivers.The 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation & Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC) on Thursday saw both sides agreeing to continue using existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander-level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC.An Indian readout also said that as a follow up to the outcomes of the 24th Special Representative talks on the boundary question last year, the two sides held detailed exchanges on issues related to boundary delimitation, border management, mechanism-building and trans-border cooperation.During SR talks, both sides had agreed to setting up an Expert Group, under WMCC, to explore Early Harvest in boundary delimitation in the India-China border areas. They had agreed to advance effective border management to maintain peace and tranquillity in respective border areas.
Article Summary: The 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation & Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC) on Thursday saw both sides agreeing to continue using existing diplomatic and military channels. India has repeatedly stressed resumption of the provision of hydrological data and other cooperation pertaining to trans-border rivers. Both sides agreed to set up an Expert Group, under WMCC, to explore Early Harvest in boundary delimitation.

Article Title: Tribunal reforms bill gets nod, paves way for national body
Article Text:
Minister of state for parliamentary affairs L Murugan informed the Rajya Sabha on Friday that the bill will be introduced in the Lok Sabha.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHIL: The Cabinet on Thursday approved the Tribunals Reforms Bill that will have the provision for setting up a National Tribunal Commission (NTC), which has been visualised as an independent body to supervise appointments and functioning of around 16 tribunals and look after their administrative and infrastructural needs.Minister of state for parliamentary affairs L Murugan informed the Rajya Sabha on Friday that the bill will be introduced in the Lok Sabha. TOI has learnt that NTC will be headed by a retired SC or high court judge for five years or till he or she turns 70 years.People aware of the proposal said the government has proposed the body at the instance of the Supreme Court The apex court had ordered the constitution of NTC first in May 2018. It reiterated its directive in 2020. In November last year, SC stressed that the government has a constitutional obligation to establish NTC and gave it four months to constitute the commission, and lamented that its directions had not been heeded.In June, the Supreme Court expressed serious concern over the functioning of tribunals across the country, with CJI Surya Kant observing that these bodies have become "a liability for the judiciary" and "a headache" for the government.The CJI had said, "Tribunals were created by you (government). So it is your headache and a liability for us. Because now the kind of orders we are seeing, barring a few tribunals, these tribunals have become a no man's land. They are not accountable to anyone."
Article Summary: The Cabinet on Thursday approved the Tribunals Reforms Bill. The bill will have the provision for setting up a National Tribunal Commission. NTC will be headed by a retired SC or high court judge for five years or till he or she turns 70 years.

Article Title: No conflict of interest in RDI Fund, says government
Article Text:
Since its establishment under an Act of Parliament in 1996, TDB has relied upon independent expert committees rather than individual officials for evaluating technology proposals

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The government on Friday said the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund is being implemented through a robust institutional framework with "stringent conflict-of-interest safeguards" in place, highlighting that it is designed "not to exclude domain expertise but to regulate it through clearly defined conflict-of-interest provisions".Rebutting a media report that 15 of the 22 entities that got public funds to boost India's deep-tech ambitions have investment links to seven members of the selection committee, raising questions of conflict of interest and propriety, Technology Development Board (TDB) secretary Rajesh Kumar Pathak said the mere existence of a professional or investment association with an innovation ecosystem entity does not constitute a violation of conflict-of-interest norms."What the framework requires is full disclosure of such interests and complete recusal from the evaluation and decision-making process relating to the proposal concerned... All members had, accordingly, recused themselves, and each decision was taken not by simple majority but by super-majority (two-thirds) of eligible members," said Pathak."Members who declare a conflict of interest neither participate in discussions nor vote on the concerned proposal."Pathak also underlined that TDB has "consistently followed similar conflict-of-interest safeguards for nearly three decades" while supporting indigenous technology development.Since its establishment under an Act of Parliament in 1996, TDB has relied upon independent expert committees rather than individual officials for evaluating technology proposals.The same institutional principles continue to govern project selection under the RDI Fund, reinforcing continuity, credibility and public confidence in the decision-making process, he added.Prof Umesh V Waghmare, secretary in the department of science and technology and TDB chairperson, said the government has followed the conflict-of-interest guidelines and framework diligently and strongly believes that there have been no violations. TDB is one of the agencies selected to grant money under the Centre's Rs 1 lakh crore RDI Fund. It has, so far, approved assistance for 22 projects involving Rs 2,192 crore of financing.
Article Summary: Technology Development Board (TDB) secretary Rajesh Kumar Pathak said the mere existence of a professional or investment association with an innovation ecosystem entity does not constitute a violation of conflict-of-interest norms. TDB is one of the agencies selected to grant money under the Centre's Rs 1 lakh crore RDI Fund. It has approved assistance for 22 projects involving Rs 2,192 crore of financing.

Article Title: Eyeing framework to regulate OTT content: I&B min
Article Text:
The panel, it said, shall devise suitable norms and guidelines 'keeping in view the cultural ethos and sensitivity of the country'

NEW DELHI: The information and broadcasting (I&B) ministry has told a parliamentary committee that it is mulling a comprehensive statutory framework to regulate the airing of programmes on OTT platforms, "which are offensive to moral standards of society", without infringing upon the rights and freedom of individuals.The department-related standing committee on the ministry of home affairs, in its recommendations in the 259th report tabled in Parliament on Friday, said the proposed comprehensive statutory framework for regulating OTT content must incorporate robust technology-enabled age verification mechanisms, effective parental controls and suitable penalties for non-compliance.While observing that the existing framework continued to rely largely on self-regulation by OTT platforms, the committee - in its recommendations on the action taken on its 254th report - reiterated that the government examine the feasibility of establishing an independent post-release review panel - comprising experts from fields like child development, education, law, social sciences and civil society - to review flagged OTT content and lay down appropriate corrective measures.The panel had, in its 254th report, said, "OTT platforms have emerged as a primary source of entertainment in India, with a reach that surpasses traditional cinema, including a substantial audience of minors." The committee pointed out that unlike films, which require mandatory pre-certification under the Cinematograph Act, OTT content operates under a self-classification system with post-release grievance redressal as per the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021.The panel said that although the aforesaid rules require age ratings, parental controls and a grievance mechanism, the lack of pre-release checks and weak age verification still leaves minors exposed to harmful content. Accordingly, it recommended that the government consider establishing a recognised panel of experts who will monitor new OTT releases.It suggested that the post-release review panel watch the flagged or trending content based on user complaints submitted through a standardised grievance mechanism.The panel, it said, shall devise suitable norms and guidelines "keeping in view the cultural ethos and sensitivity of the country". It recommended that the panel also work out suitable penalties for infringement of these norms/guidelines.
Article Summary: The information and broadcasting (I&B) ministry has told a parliamentary committee that it is mulling a comprehensive statutory framework to regulate the airing of programmes on OTT platforms. The proposed framework must incorporate robust technology-enabled age verification mechanisms, effective parental controls and suitable penalties for non-compliance.

Article Title: ‘Little hope of tracing 2 missing sailors’, Centre informs Supreme Court
Article Text:
Solicitor general (SG) Tushar Mehta told the bench that despite intense search and rescue operations, the missing Indian seafarers — Deepak Kumar Gupta and Ram Chandra Dubey — could not be located

NEW DELHI: The government informed the Supreme Court on Friday that there is very little hope of locating two Indian seafarers who are missing since the drone attack on Palau-flagged merchant ship M V AGN Ragnar on July 25 while it was departing Ukrainian waters.Filing a combined action-taken report by MEA and the Directorate General of Maritime Administration, solicitor general (SG) Tushar Mehta told the bench that despite intense search and rescue operations, the missing Indian seafarers — Deepak Kumar Gupta and Ram Chandra Dubey — could not be located.The Supreme Court told Mehta to facilitate the families’ availing maritime insurance payments.
Article Summary: The government informed the Supreme Court on Friday that there is very little hope of locating two Indian seafarers who are missing since the drone attack on Palau-flagged merchant ship M V AGN Ragnar on July 25. Article Title: NCAER: Bihar booze ban hasn't worked; lift it, fund development work
Article Text:
The paper by a team of economists led by Ratna Sahay said an end to prohibition can help the state increase its tax revenue by 14-15% while reducing expenditure on enforcement

NEW DELHI: A new paper by NCAER has proposed lifting prohibition in Bihar to generate resources for financing development and capital expenditure. It argued prohibition has not reduced crime against women and legal drinking has shifted to the consumption of illegal alcohol and drugs.The paper by a team of economists led by Ratna Sahay said an end to prohibition can help the state increase its tax revenue by 14-15% while reducing expenditure on enforcement. It also argued for more central transfers to states to help meet flood-control activities."Overall, available evidence doesn't indicate a broad-based reduction in crimes against women following prohibition. At the same time, the prohibition regime has been accompanied by concerns regarding expansion of illicit liquor trade, increased enforcement challenges and corruption, and the growing use of alternative intoxicants, including illicit drugs," the paper said, while noting a significant rise in illegal liquor trade. Presented at India Policy Forum on Friday.After returning to office on the promise of prohibition, Nitish Kumar had imposed a ban on consumption and sale of liquor in one of the most stringent regimes in the country.While the paper credits Kumar's tenure as CM for restoring law and order and getting Bihar back on the development path, it said the state still lags several other states in revenue mobilisation and depends on transfers from the Centre.The paper identified six priority areas for the state: gaps in education, gaps in health, gaps in governance and law and order, recurring floods and disasters, the missing private sector, and gender discrimination and violence. To achieve its goals, it suggested higher capex, lower subsidies, raising resources and getting more resources from the Centre.It noted that Bihar's debt burden at 39% of state GDP is higher than both high- and low-income groups, with the exception of Punjab (47%) and Bengal, which is similar. "Raising state revenues is insufficient to finance the reforms, given the state's limited taxing capacity. Additional transfers from the Centre are needed, depending on the reform," the paper said.
Article Summary: A new paper by NCAER has proposed lifting prohibition in Bihar. It argued prohibition has not reduced crime against women and legal drinking has shifted to the consumption of illegal alcohol and drugs. The paper said an end to prohibition can help the state increase its tax revenue by 14-15% while reducing expenditure on enforcement.

Article Title: India’s crude import bill up 26% in ’26-27 Q1 despite 18% volume fall
Article Text:
Russia, India's biggest supplier during the quarter, supplied crude at an average cost of $2,408 per tonne, while UAE crude cost $2,213 per tonne

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India's crude import bill rose 26% year-on-year in the first quarter of 2026-27, despite volumes falling 18%, as the West Asia conflict disrupted supplies and pushed up oil prices.Commerce department data showed India imported 59.7 million tonnes (MT) of crude between April and June this year, down from 73 MT in the corresponding period last fiscal. Import bill, however, rose to $49 billion from $39 billion in April-June 2025.India is the world's third-largest crude importer, with imports meeting 88% of annual consumption. Global oil prices, which were below $70 per barrel before the US-Iran conflict broke out in Feb, surged after shipments through the Strait of Hormuz - which handles a fifth of global oil transit - were disrupted. Around 40% of India's crude imports came through the strait from West Asian suppliers. Brent crude touched nearly $120 per barrel at the conflict's peak. The weakening rupee also added to the import bill.Since India imports 1.8-2 billion barrels of crude a year, every $1-per-barrel increase in oil prices can add up to $2 billion to its oil import bill.Average cost of crude sourced from different countries varied, partly because of differences in freight, insurance and war-risk premiums.Russia, India's biggest supplier during the quarter, supplied crude at an average cost of $2,408 per tonne, while UAE crude cost $2,213 per tonne."Our priority at that time was to secure supplies from wherever possible to ensure energy security for 1.4 billion people," said an executive of a state-run refining company, adding that discounts available before the conflict had disappeared and refiners were forced to pay hefty war-risk premiums.Russia remained India's top crude supplier in the first quarter of FY27, accounting for more than 40% of imports. UAE (14.6%), Saudi Arabia (9.9%), Venezuela (5.2%) and Oman (4.5%) were the other major suppliers.
Article Summary: India is the world's third-largest crude importer, with imports meeting 88% of annual consumption. Russia remained India's top crude supplier in the first quarter of FY27, accounting for more than 40% of imports. UAE (14.6%), Saudi Arabia (9.9%), Venezuela (5.2%) and Oman were the other major suppliers.

NEW DELHI: A parliamentary committee has recommended an integrated security and surveillance framework for all major tourist destinations in Jammu & Kashmir, incorporating comprehensive CCTV coverage, centralised monitoring facilities, regular vulnerability assessments and periodic security audits.In its 260th report tabled in Parliament on Friday, the department-related standing committee on home affairs also suggested clear inter-agency SOPs be prescribed and reviewed ahead of the peak tourist season to ensure a coordinated and timely response to any security-related incident.The recommendations, which followed the panel's visit to J&K in May 2026 to assess the security arrangements at tourist destinations, come in the wake of last year's Pahalgam terror attack in which 25 tourists were gunned down.The committee noted that sustained growth in tourist arrivals has been facilitated by improved connectivity, stronger security arrangements, better tourist infrastructure and a renewed sense of confidence among visitors."In this context, security management at tourist destinations assumes special importance, as it directly affects the perception of safety, the quality of visitor experience and the continued growth of the tourism sector," it said.Appreciating security arrangements at Gulmarg and other major tourist and religious destinations, the committee noted the deployment of security personnel, surveillance mechanisms, crowd-management measures and coordination among police, tourism department, district administration, development authorities and other agencies.

Article Title: National Handloom Day: Yogi Adityanath salutes artisans, recalls Swadeshi Movement's legacy
Article Text:
National Handloom Day: Yogi Adityanath salutes artisans, recalls Swadeshi Movement's legacy

Marking National Handloom Day, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday paid tribute to the State's weaving community, describing handloom artisans as preservers of India's cultural heritage and emphasising their role in carrying forward traditions that have been passed down through generations.Addressing a gathering in Lucknow after presenting the Sant Kabir State-Level Handloom Awards, the Chief Minister congratulated artisans across the State and linked the occasion to India's freedom movement."Today is National Handloom Day. I congratulate all the artisans across the state on Handloom Day. It was on this very day, August 7, 1905, that India's freedom struggle received a new direction," Adityanath said.He recalled that August 7 commemorates the launch of the Swadeshi Movement, which encouraged Indians to embrace indigenous products and reject foreign goods during the freedom struggle. According to the Chief Minister, the movement not only strengthened the spirit of self-reliance but also boosted confidence in India's traditional industries, particularly handloom weaving.The Chief Minister said the handloom sector is more than an economic activity.It represents India's identity, craftsmanship and cultural continuity. He stated that every handwoven fabric carries the story of the artisan behind it and reflects centuries of skill, patience and creativity.Uttar Pradesh is home to several renowned handloom traditions, including the Banarasi silk saree, Chikankari embroidery of Lucknow, Bhadohi carpets and handwoven textiles from Mau, Tanda and Mubarakpur. These crafts provide livelihoods to thousands of weaving families and contribute significantly to the state's economy and exports.Adityanath said recognising artisans through state-level awards is an effort to encourage excellence while inspiring younger generations to preserve traditional crafts. He added that supporting weavers through government initiatives, better market access and modern technology is a priority.National Handloom Day is observed every year on August 7 to commemorate the Swadeshi Movement launched in 1905. The day celebrates India's rich handloom heritage and honours millions of weavers whose craftsmanship continues to keep traditional textile arts alive despite changing market trends and industrialisation.
Article Summary: National Handloom Day is observed every year on August 7 to commemorate the Swadeshi Movement launched in 1905. The day celebrates India's rich handloom heritage and honours millions of weavers whose craftsmanship continues to keep traditional textile arts alive despite changing market trends and industrialisation.

Article Title: Past tense, eye on future: Air India hikes pilots’ pay by 8% to 15%
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Air India on Friday hiked pilot salaries by 8% to 15%, with commanders getting the biggest hikes and then the same tapering with rank. Going ahead, first officers or co-pilots will primarily get command upgrade (become captains) in AI Express (which has only single aisles) and then move to AI (which has wide body aircraft too that have higher pay) for a “strong foundation for progression within the group”. The group has tried to do multiple things — make AI Express more attractive for pilots through better pay and address shortage there mainly on the Boeing 737 fleet; check resignations and retain cockpit crew.AI pilots have for years been facing a 40 hour guaranteed pay — meaning they will get minimum for these many hours irrespective of actual flying and flying more will for more pay — while IndiGo has fixed pay for 70 hours. This has been a cause of heartburn among pilots. Under the revised framework while AI will continue to provide guaranteed pay for 40 flying hours but has enhanced flying allowance rates. Flying allowance rates beyond 40 hours have also been increased, aligning compensation with industry benchmarks while rewarding productivity.Now AI is restoring international flights that were slashed post the West Asia crisis and will return to Jan-Feb level by next month.The constraint of Pakistan airspace closure remains for Indian carriers and the longer routes they have to take for flying to and from the west — unlike direct routes taken by foreign carriers — means higher flying time and greater pilot requirement.Now a senior commander flying for about 55 hours in a month will get Rs 8.3 lakh, up from Rs 7.5 lakh at present. And a first officer doing so will get Rs 3.3 lakh, up from just over Rs 3 lakh as of now.While privilege leave has been reduced from 30 to 24, the airline will not be counting mandatory weekly off time pilots get as per regulatory requirement and the new leave structure accounts does not factor that which comes across as a cut in leave, said people in the know. IndiGo may relook at its leave policy too for pilots.Since Tata Group took over AI and AI Express in Jan 2022, the Maharaja has lost over Rs 55,000 crore due to multiple factors. The pilot pay hike announced Friday indicates it is looking at the future and preparing for growth with hundreds of aircraft on order without being bogged down by the tumultuous recent past.“New career pathways, enhanced compensation and benefits, and improved quality-of-life initiatives support Air India Group's next phase of expansion. At the heart of these initiatives is a clear, structured and transparent career pathway that provides faster command opportunities, long-term progression and access to one of the most significant widebody growth programmes in global aviation,” said an official.Since 2022, AI Group has grown from around 100 aircraft to nearly 300 aircraft and has placed orders for 600 new aircraft, including 80 wide body aircraft. Tatas are investing in capability building, including the establishment of a modern aviation academy in Gurugram with Airbus and Boeing full-flight simulators, and a new flying training school in Amravati, Maharashtra.“As AI group expands, it is focused on developing and retaining internal talent through a structured progression model across Air India Express and Air India. Pilots across Air India and Air India Express will operate under a common seniority framework, creating an integrated and transparent pathway for career progression across the group. This framework provides greater visibility into future opportunities while ensuring a consistent and structured approach to advancement,” said teh official.Under the new framework, AI Express will serve as “the primary pathway for pilots seeking command upgrades. This approach is designed to accelerate command opportunities, enable pilots to build command experience earlier in their careers, and create a strong foundation for progression within the Group.”Following command experience at AI Express, pilots will have the opportunity to progress to Air India and subsequently pursue widebody flying and command opportunities. “With 80 additional widebody aircraft on order and scheduled for induction over the coming years, Air India offers pilots a long-term pathway that is unique in the Indian market,” the official said. An additional incentive is being offered to pilots who sign up to support the growing Boeing 737 fleet in Air India Express under which they will receive a fleet allowance.
Article Summary: Air India on Friday hiked pilot salaries by 8% to 15%. commanders get the biggest hikes and then the same tapering with rank. First officers or co-pilots will primarily get command upgrade (become captains) in AI Express and then move to AI.

Article Title: India’s first satellite-guided chopper approached launched at HAL airport
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: HAL Airport in Bengaluru has become the first airport in India to operationalise a satellite-guided helicopter approach procedure, a move expected to improve safety, reduce flight times and enable more reliable all-weather operations.“The Required Navigation Performance Category H (RNP CAT H) approach, developed by the Airports Authority of India (AAI), is designed exclusively for helicopters. The procedure was validated through flight trials by HAL test pilots and approved by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA),” HAL said Friday.The new approach, it added, enables helicopters to fly highly accurate, optimised flight paths using satellite-based navigation, allowing them to safely negotiate terrain and urban obstacles while operating in adverse weather conditions.According to HAL, the procedure cuts the approach time to HAL Airport from around 12 minutes to about 4 minutes.“The operationalisation of India’s first RNP CAT H helicopter approach is a significant milestone for the country’s aviation ecosystem. This capability enhances the safety, efficiency and accessibility of helicopter operations and establishes a benchmark for similar procedures to be implemented at airports across the country,” HAL chairman and managing director Ravi K said.Besides improving safety, the system is expected to enhance operational efficiency and airspace capacity by allowing smoother integration of helicopter and fixed-wing aircraft movements. It also reduces the noise footprint over urban areas by enabling more precise flight paths.The faster approach routes are expected to benefit time-critical operations such as air ambulance services and search-and-rescue missions. HAL Airport, which handles nearly 50 helicopter movements every day, is one of the country’s busiest helicopter hubs. The introduction of the RNP CAT H procedure addresses a long-standing gap in India’s aviation infrastructure and could serve as a model for similar helicopter navigation procedures at other airports.
Article Summary: HAL Airport in Bengaluru has become the first airport in India to operationalise a satellite-guided helicopter approach procedure. The move is expected to improve safety, reduce flight times and enable more reliable all-weather operations. The new approach enables helicopters to fly highly accurate, optimised flight paths using satellite-based navigation.

Article Title: Astrobase unveils 800kN rocket engine, eyes reusability
Article Text:
Astrobase unveils India's first privately-built 800kN full-flow staged combustion rocket engine 'Everest', aiming for reusable launch systems and domestic launch infrastructure.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Space start-up Astrobase Space Technologies Friday unveiled what it described as India’s first privately built “800kN Full-Flow Staged Combustion (FFSC) liquid oxygen-methane rocket engine, named ‘Everest’”, as it seeks to develop reusable launch systems and expand domestic launch infrastructure.The Bengaluru-based company said the engine is designed for medium-lift launch vehicles and forms part of its long-term plan to build an integrated launch ecosystem covering propulsion, manufacturing, testing and launch operations. The next major milestone for the programme will be a full-engine hot-fire test, followed by vehicle integration and orbital launch development.According to the company: “Everest uses the full-flow staged combustion cycle, one of the most complex rocket engine architectures, and is powered by liquid oxygen and methane. The engine has been designed for reusability and offers 800 kN of thrust, a specific impulse of around 340 seconds and a throttle range of 50% to 110%.”The company said it plans to manufacture up to 50 engines annually once its facilities are fully operational, with the capability to hot-fire about one engine every week. It aims to test around 20 engines before attempting its first orbital mission.Its first phase of expansion is intended to support about 100 tonnes of annual launch capacity, with a longer-term goal of exceeding 1,000 tonnes through a higher launch cadence.It also said it was “working towards a launch-on-demand capability that could enable a dedicated mission within 15 days of an urgent national requirement. These targets are yet to be demonstrated”.Astrobase co-founder Neeraj Khandelwal said the engine was intended to establish an industrial capability rather than serve only as a technology demonstrator, adding that India would require indigenous high-thrust propulsion systems as satellite launches increase globally.IN-SPACe director (technical) Rajeev Jyoti said Astrobase was among the recipients of IN-SPACe’s Technology Adoption Fund, which is supporting development of the 800 kN engine. He said the programme, as it progresses through development and testing, could contribute to India’s launch capability and create new opportunities in the global space economy.Founded in 2024, Astrobase is developing propulsion systems, test infrastructure and reusable launch technologies from its Bengaluru base.
Article Summary: Astrobase Space Technologies unveils India's first privately-built 800kN full- flow staged combustion rocket engine 'Everest' The Bengaluru-based company said the engine is designed for medium-lift launch vehicles. The company said it plans to manufacture up to 50 engines annually once its facilities are fully operational.

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Friday said Congress will soon take up the issue of the Centre's E20 ethanol-blended fuel programme.In a social media post on X, Rahul shared a video and accused the government of "stealing directly out of people's pockets"."This E20 issue is a very serious matter. Usually, we say, 'Daal mein kuch kaala hai.' But here, the whole daal is black," the Congress leader said."Brothers and sisters, this is a matter of priorities. In any campaign, we have to decide the order in which issues are taken up. The problem right now is that there is so much corruption that there is a long list of issues we have to prioritise. But don't worry. We will take up the E20 issue in a big way because it is damaging people's cars and scooters and their lives and is, quite literally, stealing money directly out of their pockets," he added.The remarks came days after Congress alleged that the Centre's push for E20 petrol had increased fuel costs for consumers while primarily benefiting ethanol producers, claiming motorists were paying more despite assurances of cheaper fuel.Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said that since March 2025, regular fuel stations across the country had been supplying "practically only E20 petrol".Referring to earlier statements by Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari, he said the government had claimed ethanol blending would bring the price of diesel down to Rs 50 per litre and provide a petrol alternative at Rs 55 per litre, but no such reduction had materialised."On the contrary, according to an independent analysis, between April 2023 and March 2026, consumers collectively spent an additional approximately Rs 88,234 crore to compensate for the lower mileage from ethanol-blended fuel," he wrote in a post on X.He further claimed that the Centre could have reduced the retail price of E20 petrol to offset the lower fuel efficiency and noted that NITI Aayog's Ethanol Roadmap had recommended financial and tax incentives for E10 and E20 fuels to compensate consumers."E20 has stripped the average middle-class Indian of options, imposed higher fuel costs on them, and placed an extra burden on the very vehicle they saved for years to buy. If any segment has benefited the most from E20, it is the ethanol producers," Ramesh said.However, the Centre has maintained that ethanol blending helps reduce India's dependence on imported crude oil and supports farmers by creating demand.

Article Title: 'Do not endorse anything said': MEA rejects Bangladesh's charge over Hasina's presser
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Friday said that the India "had no role to play" in the recent media interaction made by former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina In a bi-weekly press briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that event was organised by a private entity and the government does not endorse anything said at the forum."The government had no role to play in what was an event by a private media entity." Jaiswal said."It does not endorse anything said at the forum, especially with regard to the duly constituted government of Bangladesh," he added.This comes days after Hasina, during a press conference, declared that she was determined to return to Bangladesh in December to put the country on the "right track" by restoring democracy despite the possibility of imprisonment or a death sentence."I know, they may put me in jail or kill me. I will go back home to be with my people," Hasina said."Whatever fate awaits me, I will return to my people. I cannot stay away while my beloved countrymen are suffering," she said.Hasina alleged that the July-August 2024 protests that led to the fall of her government were not a spontaneous student movement but were orchestrated by organised groups to create a path to power outside the electoral process.Reacting strongly to the media interaction, Bangladesh's foreign ministry said it was "outraged" that the event had been allowed despite Dhaka raising concerns with New Delhi over its potential impact on bilateral ties."Bangladesh is outraged that the absconding convicted genocider Sheikh Hasina was allowed this evening to engage in a live interaction with the media in New Delhi, where she and her henchmen launched venomous vitriol against the State of Bangladesh and its people," the ministry said in a statement.Describing the event as "an affront to the sovereignty of Bangladesh", the ministry alleged that Hasina and her associates had used Indian soil to launch "venomous vitriol" against Bangladesh and its people.Reiterating its position, the foreign ministry said Bangladesh remained committed to building a constructive and mutually beneficial relationship with India based on sovereign equality, mutual respect, non-interference and national dignity.Dhaka also urged India to clarify its policy towards Bangladesh.Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaed said New Delhi must decide whether it would continue to allow Awami League leaders to "carry out conspiratorial activities" from its territory."India is a democratic country. India itself has to decide what its foreign policy will be regarding Bangladesh. We want good relations in the interest of the people of both countries," she said."But the relationship has to be based on equality, mutual respect and safeguarding each country's interests. If India understands that, it will be good for everyone," she added.
Article Summary: MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that event was organised by a private entity and the government does not endorse anything said at the forum. Bangladesh's foreign ministry said it was "outraged" that the event had been allowed despite Dhaka raising concerns.
